title: The Cech resolution and derived direct image
statement:
Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, let $f:X\to S$ be a separated,
quasi-compact morphism, and choose a finite affine open cover
$X=\bigcup_{i=1}^t U_i$. For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module
$\mathcal F$, write $U_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}U_j$ and $j_J:U_J\to X$.
The augmented alternating Cech complex of sheaves

$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal F\longrightarrow
\prod_i j_{i,*}(\mathcal F|_{U_i})\longrightarrow
\prod_{i<j}j_{ij,*}(\mathcal F|_{U_{ij}})\longrightarrow\cdots
$$

is exact. Its non-augmented terms are $f_*$-acyclic, so applying
$f_*$ to it computes $Rf_*\mathcal F$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-cech-sheaf-resolution] to the open cover and F. This constructs D, epsilon and the sectionwise isomorphisms, verifies the differential and augmentation formulas, identifies each term as the product of open direct images, and gives QuasiIso epsilon. This step does not assume finiteness or quasi-coherence.

X is separated absolutely because its map to the affine Spec A is separated. For every tuple y:Fin(p+1)->I the finite nonempty intersection of U(y(l)) is affine [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection], iterated by Mathlib IsAffineOpen.iInf. Apply [lem-pc-affine-open-pushforward-acyclic] to obtain classical f_*-acyclicity of each factor. The rightAcyclic property contains zero and is stable under binary products and isomorphisms. Mathlib ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderFiniteProducts.mk' and prop_product therefore give acyclicity of the finite product, including the empty index set. Transport through the term isomorphism to get acyclicity of D^p.

The ringed-space module category is Grothendieck abelian [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], hence has enough injectives. The homology comparison with the classical right derived functors, from [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility], gives the specified vanishing of schemeModuleHigherDirectImage in every positive natural degree.

Extend D and epsilon from natural to integer degrees by zero. The extension is bounded below and its terms remain acyclic, because the property contains zero and is stable under isomorphisms. Apply the source-library acyclic unit theorem isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_of_rightAcyclic (the unit form of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity]) to this bounded-below complex. By [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility] the unbounded right derived functor on QD is isomorphic to the inclusion of its bounded-below right derived functor. Invert the acyclic unit and compose the quotient factorization isomorphisms to obtain Rf_*(QD) isomorphic to Q(f_*D). Extension preserves the quasi-isomorphism epsilon and extension of a single complex is a single complex, so Qepsilon identifies F[0] with QD. Apply Rf_* to that isomorphism and compose. No bounded-above or finite-length claim for the full Cech complex is made.
